Subject: Radar scan: pricing & model-release signals — QBR prep

Team,

Ahead of the QBR next week I pulled together a short radar scan of external signals that should shape our competitive narrative and the slides we bring. High level notes below — attached is a csv export (pricing-moves-1129.csv) and a two-page model timeline (model-release-timeline-1129.pdf).

1) Pricing moves
- "Nimbus AI" cut per-token list pricing by ~15% for their hosted text-gen endpoints (announced 11/28). Field reports show reps nudging prospects on cost comparisons.
- "CloudWeave" introduced a consumption credit for first 90 days on Dedicated equivalents — seems targeted at mid-market procurement cycles.

2) Model releases & packaging
- "Helio-30B" (open-ish 30B family) announced faster latencies and a new 4-bit quant profile; early benchmarks suggest throughput improvements at lower memory cost. Expect partner messaging pivots around latency and TCO.
- Several smaller vendors are surfacing model variants that bundle embeddings + cheap reranking as a packaged offering.

3) Positioning shifts to watch
- Competitors leaning into "predictable unit economics" messaging — essentially our space but without the operational guarantees we provide.
- Increased emphasis on regionally hosted private instances for EU customers; CloudWeave highlighted data residency in recent blog.

QBR asks (short):
- Please review slides draft linked in Drive and flag any missing signals (I set a change window until Tue EOD).
- Agree top-3 competitive risks we should put on the exec slide (pricing pressure, model parity, regional compliance).
- Confirm who on the leadership panel will handle pricing talk vs. product/tech tradeoffs.

Attachments: pricing-moves-1129.csv, model-release-timeline-1129.pdf, QBR-slides-draft.pptx (draft)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QBRradar2026

Thanks — short read, no action required unless you want to swap ownership of a bullet.

— Olga
